sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: FLAG tag at N-terminus: ANP EC50 and kinetics of guanylyl cyclase activation unchanged (Schröter et al., 2010, cited in L3). HA tag at N-terminus of mouse NPR1 (L1/L2): full-length receptor detected by western blot at expected molecular weight in multiple tissues; guanylyl cyclase activity not separately reported for the HA knock-in.
sites.rationale: The signal peptide spans residues 1–32 (landmark-authoritative); the mature extracellular domain begins at G33. A tag placed upstream of residue 33 would be cleaved with the signal peptide, so the only valid extracellular N-terminal junction is insert_after_residue=32 (between A32 and G33). No clip names a specific residue number, so the position is topology-derived from the single extracellular N-terminus. L3 provides the strongest functional evidence: FLAG at this position leaves ANP-stimulated GC activity and kinetics intact. L1 independently confirms the position is tolerated in vivo via CRISPR knock-in of HA at the same terminus in mouse NPR1 (a close ortholog). L4/L5 confirm the same N-terminal FLAG strategy on full-length human NPR1 in a membrane-anchored expression system. L3 (PMC9627482) reports that a FLAG epitope tag (DYKDDDDK) added to the N-terminus of full-length, membrane-anchored NPR1 had no effect on ANP-dependent guanylyl cyclase activation or kinetics (Schröter et al., 2010), cited in the context of validating the HA-NPR1 knock-in strategy. L1 (same paper) reports an HA tag (YPYDVPDYA) inserted at the extracellular N-terminus of endogenous mouse NPR1 by CRISPR/Cas9 knock-in, confirmed by western blot at the expected ~120–130 kDa (L2). L4/L5 (PMC12493526, PMC13230927) report full-length human NPR1/GC-A expressed with an N-terminal FLAG tag in a membrane-anchored pFastBac1 construct.

sources.claim: A previous study demonstrated that addition of an epitope tag of similar size (FLAG, DYKDDDDK) to the N-terminus of NPR1 had no effect on the ANP concentration required to activate NPR1 guanylyl cyclase activity, or on the kinetics of the activation ( Schröter et al., 2010 ).

literature_notes: Six ledger lines were evaluated. L1, L2, L3, L4, and L5 all converge on the same site: an epitope tag at the extracellular N-terminus of NPR1, after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 32. Because they all pin the identical junction (topology-derived: insert_after_residue=32), they constitute one site, not multiple; L3 was chosen as the primary clip because it carries explicit functional validation (GC activity unchanged). L6 reports a C-terminal GFP fusion on full-length human GC-A expressed in CHO-K1 cells; per the authoritative topology landmarks the C-terminus (residues 495–1061) is entirely intracellular, so this is recorded in other_positions rather than sites. No ledger line reports a tolerated insertion in any internal extracellular loop of NPR1, so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: L6 reports a C-terminal GFP fusion on full-length human GC-A (NPR1) confirmed at the cell surface in CHO-K1 cells; however, the authoritative topology places the entire C-terminal domain (residues 495–1061) intracellularly, so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface-display site.
